At dusk outside ancient Nineveh’s wall, Tobit a middle-aged Jewish exile in modest rough robes respectfully lowers a completely wrapped linen shroud into a prepared simple grave, with one quiet helper. No exposed corpse or injuries, no crucifixes, no modern cemetery. Compassionate sober act, coherent arms and hands, lamp and digging tool nearby.
